text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan is set to decide on his conservative coalition partner's proposal to extend the one-and-a-half day new year holiday to five days including the weekend.
- France, Italy and Spain promise Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller backing for Turkey's bid for full membership of the European Union.
- Iraqi Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani has sent a letter to the Turkey-based guerrilla Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) asking for help for peace in turbulent nothern Iraq.
- Foreign minister Tansu Ciller says she will be prime minister in 1998 taking her term under the coalition deal in her visit to Dublin.
- Human right groups say the doctors in Turkey are under the pressure to give health reports who conceal evidence of torture.
- A contemporary lawyer's organisation asks for change in the constitution enabling women to keep her maiden name after getting married.
- Energy minister says that Turkey has signed contracts for the import of a total 31 billion cubic metres of natural gas.
- Turkish armed forces conducts a survey among its southeast based staff in order to shape its strategy in its fight against PKK rebels.
- The loading of the first Iraqi oil into tankers at the Turkish port of Ceyhan to be celebrated with ceremonies on Monday.
